analysis.title: Morning Market Tidbits: Will the blue wave sweep tariffs away?
key_insights: Tariffs contributed to the affordability concerns that appear to have played a major role in the midterm results.
BofA sees no near-term tariff relief from the midterm outcome, because Congress has ceded control of trade policy to the executive branch.
With a $2tn deficit, BofA sees only modest scope for tariffs (about $300bn of revenue) to be rolled back, and not before 2029.
Tariffs raised about $310bn in the last 12 months, nearly 1% of GDP. Of that, $126bn came from China, Southeast Asia and India, and BofA expects those tariffs to most likely stay.
Traditional US allies (EU, Canada, Mexico, Japan, Korea) account for over $100bn of tariff revenue (0.3% of GDP) and are the most likely candidates for relief.
BofA's 3Q26 GDP tracking estimate rose one tenth to 3.8% q/q saar after the September trade balance, against an official BofA 3Q forecast of 3.4%.

Today's calendar: jobless claims, nonfarm productivity, unit labor costs, and comments from Fed officials Hammack, Barkin and Logan. BofA expects 3Q productivity of 4.8% against 2.7% consensus and unit labor costs of -1.3% against 0.5% consensus.

tension_points.bull_case: Tariffs fed the affordability concerns that appear to have driven the midterm results, so a future administration or Congress could roll some back, mainly for traditional allies (EU, Canada, Mexico, Japan, Korea, over $100bn of revenue).
tension_points.bear_case: A $2tn deficit means the government cannot afford to lose roughly $300bn of tariff revenue, and the $126bn from China, Southeast Asia and India will most likely stick.
tension_points.what_invalidates: BofA says Congress has ceded trade policy to the executive branch, so near-term relief depends on the administration. It sees modest rollback only after 2028.

theme_stances.key_argument: Given the $2tn deficit, there is only modest scope for tariffs to be rolled back after 2028.
theme_stances.evidence: we see only modest scope for tariffs to get rolled back
